newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to spend $625 million on engines.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to spend $625 million on engines.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Wednesday it plans to spend $625 million to introduce its first family of all-aluminum V-6 engines next year.

Chrysler said the new engines, which will power its next generation 1998 Dodge Intrepid, Chrysler Concorde, Chrysler LHS and Eagle Vision cars, are 10 percent more fuel efficient, and 25 percent more powerful than the engines they replace.
Much of the investments will go to upgrade the plants that will build the engines, in Kenosha, Wis., and Trenton, Mich.
Kenosha will build about 400,000 2.7-litre engines annually, while Trenton will produce about 240,000 3.2-litre and 3.5 litre engines annually.

The Kenosha-made dual overhead cam engines, which produce 200 horsepower, will replace cast-iron 3.3-litre V6 as the base engine in the Intrepid and Concorde. They also will be used in other Chrysler vehicles, a company spokesman said.
The engines were developed in 24 months, much faster than the five years needed for many other engine programmes, which often approach investments of $1 billion.
The 220-horsepower 3.2-litre engine will power the Concorde LXI and Intrepid ES models, while the 250-horsepower 3.5-litre engine will appear in the Chrysler LHS and Eagle Vision cars.
Volume production of the engines will begin in August 1997.
Chrysler's stock rose 62.5 cents to $33.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
